purpose: Cross-check the six scientific-name labels in Quimpang et al. (2018) against Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes, preserving the source table spelling and not treating name status as sample re-identification.

authority.name: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes
authority.institution: California Academy of Sciences, Institute for Biodiversity Science and Sustainability
authority.versionObserved: The selected indexed Catalog records display an online version updated 13 August 2026.
authority.accessMethod: Exact-name records were reviewed through indexed excerpts from official Catalog pages. Direct opens of some selected records returned access errors; no challenge or access control was bypassed.
authority.reuse: No item-specific permission to republish Catalog text was verified. Only brief attributed nomenclatural outcomes and links are recorded; no bulk export or catalogue text is reproduced.

nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: The Catalog lists Cyprinus carpio as valid and notes that the trinomial subspecies form C. carpio carpio is used in some literature.
nameCrosswalk.disposition: Preserve the source trinomial. Do not infer a specific domesticated/wild strain or specimen identity from the name form.

nameCrosswalk.sourceLabel: Xiphophorus helleri (Heckel, 1848) in Table 3; Figure 3 caption prints X. hellerii
nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: The Catalog recognizes Xiphophorus hellerii as valid. The paper's Table 3 uses the single-i spelling helleri while its Figure 3 caption uses hellerii.
nameCrosswalk.disposition: This resolves a source-spelling inconsistency as a candidate nomenclatural form only; no specimen was reidentified.

interpretation.taxonomy: Five binomial labels match current Catalog names; the sixth, Cyprinus carpio carpio, is retained as the source's subspecies-form usage while the Catalog accepts Cyprinus carpio at species level. Xiphophorus has a documented table-versus-figure spelling difference.
interpretation.specimenIdentity: The authority cross-check validates nomenclatural forms only. No voucher accession, specimen, image or tissue was available for independent identification.
interpretation.localPresence: Catalog names, broad distributions and type details do not validate the article's 2013 fish identifications, lake/outlet provenance or current local presence.
interpretation.nonIndigenousStatus: The article's historical two-native/four-exotic classification is not independently reassessed here and is not admitted as current non-native status or impact evidence.
interpretation.publication: Taxonomic name status does not approve reuse of the paper's table, photographs, occurrence claims or derived app content.

limitations: The paper's Results prose assigns Xiphophorus helleri and X. maculatus to the outlet stream, but the table does not fully allocate the remaining taxa between lake and outlet; nomenclature cannot supply that missing station crosswalk.
The article provides no accession numbers or repository crosswalk for the up-to-five preserved samples per species.
A potentially overlapping 2015 Lake Duminagat survey by overlapping authors remains unresolved; this taxonomy screen does not merge its names or samples.
Only selected Catalog name-status records are used; no current presence, introduction pathway, ecological impact, diet, safety or legal claim is inferred.

references.supports: Table 3 and Figure 3 name forms and the Xiphophorus spelling variant.
